hypothesis: Converting planar int4 RAM blocks into the device's signed pairs while staging lets the CUDA chain promote experts with the default planar CPU kernel, raising decode on a card that holds only part of the experts.
command: make -C c qwen36 CUDA=1 CUDA_ARCH=sm_89; COLI_CUDA=1 COLI_GPUS=0 HEAT_FILE=<a copy of the frozen heat file> CUDA_EXPERT_GB=5 OMP_NUM_THREADS=6 OMP_WAIT_POLICY=ACTIVE OMP_PROC_BIND=close SNAP=<model> COLI_TEMP=0 COLI_TIMERS=1 NOSTREAM=1 N_NEW=200 ./c/qwen36 256 4 prompt_story_short.txt

hardware.cpu: Intel Xeon @ 2.20GHz (6 cores / 12 threads, 38.5 MiB L3) + NVIDIA L4 (23034 MiB, sm_89)
hardware.storage: Google Colab VM disk (model copied to /content/models before the runs)

quality.method: make -C c check; tests/test_qwen36_tier_promote on the L4 with and without AVX2; greedy text bit-identical to origin/dev with every expert in VRAM (CUDA_EXPERT_GB=auto) and with COLI_CUDA_CHAIN_PROMOTE=0; at CUDA_EXPERT_GB=5 the greedy text parts (a promoted expert runs the card's kernel instead of the CPU's), so quality is the teacher-forced loss (PPL=1): 3.0719 nats/token with promotion against 3.0774 without and 3.0725 with every expert in VRAM (600-token prose, 250 scored)
